q: In December 2001, actress Winona Ryder was arrested after shoplifting more than $5,500 worth of designer merchandise from which Beverly Hills department store?
options: Barneys New York during the notorious incident
fact: Ryder was convicted in 2002 of grand theft and vandalism for cutting security tags off luxury items at Saks Fifth Avenue on Wilshire Boulevard.

q: In 1994, comedian Bobcat Goldthwait shocked host Jay Leno and the studio audience on "The Tonight Show" by doing what right before leaving the stage?
options: Dousing the guest armchair with lighter fluid and setting it on fire
Smashing an electric guitar over the guest desk
Handcuffing himself to Leno's microphone stand
Diving headfirst into the studio orchestra's drum kit
fact: Goldthwait soaked the chair and ignited it on the May 1994 broadcast; he was later fined and ordered to film public service announcements about fire safety.

q: In 2007, Nicolas Cage outbid Leonardo DiCaprio at an auction to buy a 67-million-year-old dinosaur skull, only to discover later that it was:
options: A fiberglass replica made for a natural history museum
Illegally smuggled out of the Gobi Desert in Mongolia
Radioactive due to nearby uranium mining deposits
Part of a catalog stolen from the British Museum
fact: Cage voluntarily agreed to repatriate the Tyrannosaurus bataar skull in 2015 after US Department of Homeland Security investigators confirmed it had been stolen from Mongolia.

q: Elvis Presley was infamous for impulsively destroying appliances at Graceland. What did he notoriously do whenever entertainer Robert Goulet appeared on television?
options: Dumped sweet tea into the back chassis vents
Shot the television screen with a handgun
Had his Memphis Mafia throw it into the pool
Smashed the picture tube with a hollow-body guitar
fact: Elvis maintained a deep, unexplained distaste for Robert Goulet and shot multiple television sets across his home whenever Goulet’s face flashed on the screen.

q: In October 1999, police in Austin, Texas, arrested Matthew McConaughey following a 3:00 AM noise complaint after finding him doing what in his home?
options: Throwing antique furniture off his second-story balcony
Firing a blank pistol from his back porch at raccoons
Dancing naked and playing the bongo drums
Hosting an unsanctioned rooftop arm-wrestling contest
fact: Officers dispatched to McConaughey's house found him dancing in the buff and banging on bongos with another man present; charges were eventually reduced to a noise fine.

q: During a January 1982 performance in Des Moines, Iowa, Ozzy Osbourne was rushed to get rabies shots after he:
options: Allowed a swarm of live bees to crawl over his hands
Drank water directly from a drainage ditch outside the arena
Bit the head off a real bat thrown onto the stage
Bit into a taxidermied fox brought backstage
fact: Osbourne believed the bat was a rubber stage prop until it moved inside his mouth, leading to an immediate emergency trip to Broadlawns Medical Center.

q: Which surrealist master famously walked a pet anteater on a leash down public Parisian boulevards and took it aboard the Paris Métro in 1969?
fact: Dalí was widely photographed walking his pet giant anteater through Paris, fitting his lifelong theatrical flair for surrealist self-promotion.

q: Bill Murray famously does not employ a talent agent, manager, or publicist. How have Hollywood directors traditionally reached him to pitch roles?
options: By mailing scripts to a PO Box in Charleston, South Carolina
By leaving a voicemail on an unmonitored 1-800 toll-free phone number
By sending telegrams to a local golf clubhouse
By paging his personal attorney via an encoded fax line
fact: Filmmakers from Sofia Coppola to Wes Anderson had to leave pitches on Murray’s mysterious 1-800 voice mailbox, which he checks only sporadically.

q: In 1989, Keith Richards reportedly pulled a switchblade backstage during the Rolling Stones' "Steel Wheels" tour and threatened to carve up which future US President if he did not vacate their private room?
fact: Trump had co-promoted the Stones' Atlantic City pay-per-view gig under the condition he would not attend the Stones' personal press conference; when he showed up anyway, Richards pulled his knife and ordered him out.

q: In the mid-1970s, during his cocaine-fueled "Thin White Duke" period in Los Angeles, David Bowie reportedly stored what in his home freezer out of paranoia that witches would steal his essence?
fact: Biographers, including Christopher Sandford, noted Bowie's profound occult paranoia at the time, which included storing his own urine in jars in the freezer to ward off witches.

q: What eccentric request did Van Halen famously include in their concert riders to verify that promoters had read all their safety and technical requirements?
options: A room painted entirely in matte chalkboard black
A bowl of M&Ms with all the brown ones removed
Exactly three cases of warm Dr Pepper
An oxygen tank behind the drum kit
fact: Singer David Lee Roth devised the brown M&M clause as a rapid canary in the coal mine; if he spotted brown M&Ms backstage, he knew the promoter hadn't read their heavy production rigging requirements.

q: In 1973, Marlon Brando declined his Academy Award for Best Actor for "The Godfather" and sent which Native American civil rights activist to read a protest statement in his place?
fact: Littlefeather appeared in traditional Apache dress to deliver Brando's statement condemning the depiction of Native Americans in film and drawing attention to the Wounded Knee occupation.

q: Which action film icon was famously choked unconscious by judo master Gene LeBell on a movie set after claiming his martial arts made him impervious to chokes?
fact: On the set of "Out for Justice" (1991), Seagal reportedly bragged no one could choke him out; LeBell took the challenge, choked Seagal out, and rumors long circulated that Seagal lost bowel control.

q: In 1993, while on a flight from Los Angeles to New York, musician and actor Courtney Love was arrested upon landing at Heathrow Airport after:
options: Smuggling an endangered cockatoo inside her handbag
Smashing a business class television monitor with a shoe
Lighting a cigarette in the lavatory and triggering the fire alarm during the notorious incident
Verbally abusing the cabin crew and refusing to sit during landing
fact: Love was arrested by British police in February 2003 for using threatening, abusive words after an altercation over cabin seating instructions on a Virgin Atlantic flight.

q: What did British eccentric Keith Moon, the legendary drummer of The Who, once do to an entire hotel bathroom using cherry bombs and dynamite?
options: Blew the sink out into the hallway
Obliterated the floor, causing the bathtub to fall into the room below
Shattered every mirror and tile along all four walls
Blew the porcelain toilet to pieces
fact: Moon was infamous for flushing high-grade explosives down hotel toilets; on his 21st birthday in Flint, Michigan, he blew a toilet to smithereens with cherry bombs.

q: In 2014, while starring in "Cabaret" on Broadway, Shia LaBeouf was arrested during a performance of the musical after:
options: Storming the stage demanding to sing the final song
Climbing onto the lighting rig during the opening number
Throwing playbills onto the orchestra pit from the front mezzanine
Slapping actor Alan Cumming on the rear and shouting obscenities
fact: LaBeouf disrupted the first act of "Cabaret" at Studio 54 by smoking, yelling, and swatting Alan Cumming's backside as Cumming walked through the aisle.

q: Which Golden Age Hollywood screen legend reportedly bathed exclusively in Evian water and refused to drink tap water under any circumstances?
fact: In the 1990s, Kim Basinger's rider famously leaked revealing she insisted on washing her hair exclusively in bottled Evian mineral water.

q: What bizarre vehicle did rapper Snoop Dogg attempt to rent when visiting the Principality of Liechtenstein in 2010 to shoot a music video?
options: The Prince's personal gold-plated helicopter during the notorious incident
The entire sovereign country of Liechtenstein
fact: Snoop attempted to rent out the entire microstate of Liechtenstein for a promotional video, but his booking request was denied because local officials were not given enough advance notice.

q: Which pop diva famously demanded in a tour rider that her dressing room contain 20 white kittens and 100 white doves?
fact: While switching on the Christmas lights at London's Westfield mall in 2009, Carey reportedly requested 20 white kittens and 100 doves, though organizers had to reject the request on health and safety grounds.

q: In 2005, author Hunter S. Thompson had his cremated ashes fired from a 153-foot cannon shaped like a double-thumbed fist. Who funded the lavish $3 million funeral?
fact: Depp, who portrayed Thompson in "Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas" and became a close personal friend, financed the construction of the massive cannon tower on Thompson's farm in Woody Creek, Colorado.

q: What did musician Jack White do when a local radio station leaked tracks from his album "Blunderbuss" in 2012 before its release date?
options: Sued the station for copyright infringement
Recorded a 15-minute spoken word rant and personally hand-delivered the vinyl
Played a free guerrilla concert directly on the station's front lawn
Personally bought the radio station and changed its format to talk radio
fact: White has frequently pulled guerrilla stunts; on several occasions, when frustrated by radio or press incidents, he staged unannounced pop-up shows outside studios and venues.

q: In 1975, which famous director threw a glass of champagne into critic John Simon’s face after Simon wrote a savage review of his wife's Broadway performance?
fact: Bogdanovich was so enraged by Simon's vicious personal attacks on his partner Cybill Shepherd that he tossed a full glass of champagne into Simon's face in a theater lobby.

q: Which legendary British actor insisted on wearing his full Roman centurion armor costume to a local pub during breaks while filming "The Life of Brian"?
fact: Graham Chapman, who was also an active mountaineer and medical doctor, frequently wandered off in full costume—drinking gin and tonic at village bars dressed as Brian or an officer.

q: Why did actor Christopher Walken spend weeks working as an assistant lion tamer in a traveling circus when he was 16 years old?
options: He joined a circus troupe during summer break and performed with a lioness named Sheba
He was fulfilling community service for joyriding
He was doing deep method research for an off-Broadway play
His uncle owned the circus and forced him to work the menagerie
fact: Before finding acting fame, a teenage Walken worked for the Terrell Jacobs circus outfit, performing alongside an elderly, docile lioness named Sheba.

q: In 1995, which actress famously arrived at the 67th Academy Awards in a white boy's undershirt from the Gap paired with an Armani skirt?
fact: Stone mixed high-and-low fashion after a dry cleaner ruined her intended designer gown right before the ceremony, prompting her to grab a simple ribbed Gap tee from her closet.

q: Which rock icon allegedly snorted a line of his own father's cremated ashes mixed with cocaine?
fact: Richards admitted in an interview with NME in 2007 that he snorted a tiny pinch of his father Bert's ashes, though he later clarified he planted an English oak tree over the rest.

q: What unusual item did actor Danny DeVito carry everywhere on the set of "Batman Returns" to remain fully in character as the Penguin?
options: A dead mackerel inside his coat pocket
A customized monocle permanently glued to his eye
Rotten fish guts in a vial
fact: DeVito fully embraced the grim nature of the Penguin, chewing on real raw fish and keeping dead fish in his pockets to smell revolting to his co-stars.

q: Which pop superstar was pulled over by German customs officials in 2013 for attempting to bring an undocumented capuchin monkey named "OG Mally" into the country?
fact: Bieber's capuchin monkey was seized at Munich Airport when he failed to present vaccination and import paperwork; the monkey was eventually rehomed in a German zoo.

q: In 1986, which screen legend famously showed up on the set of "The Island of Dr. Moreau" wearing an ice bucket on his head because he felt the temperature was uncomfortably hot?
fact: During the notoriously chaotic 1996 filming of "The Island of Dr. Moreau", Brando refused to take direction and famously placed an ice bucket atop his head between takes to stay cool.

q: In 2001, which Oscar-winning actor bought an entire ghost town in Georgia named Braselton for $20 million, intending to build movie studios and a theme park?
fact: Basinger bought Braselton, Georgia in 1989 for $20 million hoping to turn it into a tourist destination, but financial troubles later forced her to sell it at a massive loss.

q: Which musician had his severed finger reattached after a bizarre 1978 gardening mishap where he severed it with hand hedge trimmers?
fact: Jerry Garcia famously lost two-thirds of his right middle finger at age four when his brother accidentally chopped it with an axe while cutting wood on a camping trip.

q: In 1971, which member of Led Zeppelin drove a rented sports car through the lobby of the Edgewater Inn hotel in Seattle?
fact: Drummer John Bonham was legendary for destroying hotel rooms and rental vehicles; he actually drove a rented motorcycle down the hallways and lobby of the Edgewater Inn.

q: Which movie star spent a night in jail in Japan in 1980 after customs agents discovered nearly a half-pound of marijuana in his luggage?
fact: McCartney spent nine days in Tokyo's Narcotics Detention Center after customs officers discovered 7.7 ounces of pot packed in his suitcase ahead of Wings' Japanese tour.

q: What did eccentric billionaire Howard Hughes famously do when Baskin-Robbins discontinued his favorite flavor, banana ripple?
options: Sued the company for breach of an oral contract
Purchased a franchise store and forced them to keep churning it
Ordered 350 gallons specially made, then lost interest after one scoop
Sent chemists to reverse-engineer the artificial flavor formula
fact: Hughes’ aides ordered an entire batch of 350 gallons from Baskin-Robbins; as soon as it arrived at his hotel in Las Vegas, Hughes announced he was tired of it and wanted vanilla instead.

q: Which Hollywood actor broke into an elderly neighbor's home while intoxicated in 1996 and fell asleep in an 11-year-old child's bed?
fact: At the height of his substance abuse struggles, Downey wandered into his neighbor's Malibu home by mistake and passed out in an unoccupied child's bedroom.

q: In 1968, which member of The Beatles accidentally left his lyric notebook containing early drafts of "Hey Jude" in the back of a London taxi?
fact: McCartney once misplaced his notebook with handwritten lines for "Hey Jude" in a cab; the cabbie recognized it and returned the priceless papers to Apple Corps.

q: Which actress famously broke her ankle during the filming of "The Silence of the Lambs" because she was running too hard down the basement set stairs?
fact: Brooke Smith, who played captive Catherine Martin, was so terrified and immersed while shooting Buffalo Bill's basement scenes that she severely twisted and sprained her ankle.

q: In 1994, which actor tackled an armed mugger trying to rob a woman in Manhattan, only to discover the "mugger" was a stunt actor on a television shoot?
fact: Harrelson tackled an apparent purse-snatcher on a New York sidewalk before crew members frantically screamed that they were filming an episode of "New York Undercover".

q: What did Salvador Dalí do to avoid paying large dinner bills at lavish restaurants with friends?
options: Drew surrealist sketches on the back of his payment checks so no one would cash them
Slipped a dried beetle into his final course
Claimed to be the Emperor of Austria and immune to commercial debt
Paid exclusively with customized fake dollar bills stamped with his mustache
fact: Dalí knew that restaurant owners would rather frame a signed original sketch on a paper check than cash it for a few hundred dollars, effectively scoring him free meals.

q: Which pop icon sent a personalized floral arrangement shaped like a giant middle finger to a music executive after getting out of an unwanted contract?
fact: After contentious legal battles with Warner Bros. where he wrote "SLAVE" on his cheek, Prince was known to send cutting, symbolic gestures and sculptures to studio brass.

q: In 2012, which movie star called a real emergency locksmith to help him break into his own house after forgetting his keys, then signed the invoice with an alien sketch?
fact: Goldblum famously chatted with the locksmith about extraterrestrial life and signed the paperwork with an impromptu drawing of a space alien.

q: Which iconic rock frontman famously challenged a professional sumo wrestler to an impromptu match backstage in Tokyo in 1990 and was instantly tossed across the room?
fact: Axl Rose was introduced to a towering Japanese sumo champion during Guns N' Roses' tour in Tokyo and insisted on sparring, resulting in Rose immediately getting thrown onto a sofa.

q: In 1970, which singer met President Richard Nixon in the Oval Office and requested an official badge from the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs?
fact: Elvis wrote a handwritten five-page letter to Nixon on American Airlines stationery requesting a federal narcotics badge, which Nixon happily presented to him during their meeting.

q: Which actor reportedly wore a pair of high heels and full vampire fangs around his house for two months to prepare for a role?
fact: Oldman immersed himself in the eccentric mannerisms of Count Dracula for Francis Ford Coppola's 1992 film, including wearing historical platform shoes and prosthetic teeth off-camera.

q: In 1985, which pop star secretly bought the Beatles' catalog publishing rights for $47.5 million, permanently straining his close friendship with Paul McCartney?
fact: McCartney had casually explained the lucrative value of music publishing to Jackson; months later, Jackson went behind McCartney's back to purchase ATV Music, owning the Lennon-McCartney library.

q: What did actor Christopher Lee do on the set of "The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers" when director Peter Jackson tried to give him notes on the sound of a man being stabbed in the back?
options: Walked off set and refused to return for three days
Asked Jackson if he had ever butchered livestock
Laughed and challenged Jackson to a duel with prop daggers
Told Jackson he already knew what sound it made from his secret WWII service
fact: Lee corrected Jackson on the sound someone makes when stabbed in the back, bluntly reminding him of his classified Special Operations Executive (SOE) service in World War II.

q: In 1997, which actor accidentally sank a $450,000 McLaren F1 supercar into a hedge while driving near Marlborough, England?
fact: Atkinson ("Mr. Bean"), an avid petrolhead and racing enthusiast, crashed his ultra-rare McLaren F1 twice—once in 1999 and again in 2011, securing one of the largest auto insurance payouts in British history.

q: Which Hollywood actress once walked away from a pet store with an African lion cub named Neil, who subsequently lived inside her Los Angeles family home and slept in her bed?
fact: Tippi Hedren and husband Noel Marshall brought a 400-pound lion named Neil to live in their Sherman Oaks house before producing their disastrous animal movie "Roar".

q: Which famous guitarist built a full-scale replica of a 19th-century pirate ship in his backyard, complete with working cannons?
fact: Richards indulged his obsession with classic pirates and maritime lore by commissioning elaborate pirate-themed installations and armaments across his country estate.

q: In 2003, which eccentric pop star attended a formal press conference wearing a surgical mask and holding an open umbrella indoors?
fact: Jackson routinely made public appearances in the early 2000s shielding his skin and respiratory system from light and germs using parasols, blankets, and surgical masks.

q: In 1976, Elvis Presley flew his private Lisa Marie jet from Memphis to Denver and back in the middle of the night just to eat what legendary sandwich?
options: A foot-long fried catfish po'boy with jalapeño slaw
The Fool's Gold Loaf: an entire hollow-out sourdough loaf stuffed with peanut butter, blueberry jam, and bacon
A quadruple-decker hot pastrami on pumpernickel from a 24-hour deli
A deep-fried breakfast burrito smothered in green chile
fact: Elvis and his entourage flew over 1,000 miles to Denver's Stapleton Airport, where owners of the Colorado Mine Company brought 22 Fool's Gold Loaves directly to the hangar tarmac.

q: What bizarre condition did Marlon Brando demand while negotiating his brief cameo as Jor-El in 1978's "Superman"?
options: He suggested Jor-El could look like a glowing green bagel so he wouldn't have to appear in person
He refused to memorize lines and insisted on reading his dialogue off baby Superman’s diapers
He demanded that his voice be run through a synthesizer to disguise his identity
fact: Brando famously proposed Jor-El appear as a talking bagel or suitcase to avoid filming in costume, and he read his lines off cue cards hidden on set—including on the infant Kal-El's diaper.

q: During the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards, why did Rage Against the Machine bassist Tim Commerford climb onto a 20-foot scaffold structure on stage?
options: To perform a planned acoustic solo from the lighting rig
To hang an anti-war banner over the podium
Because the stage pyrotechnics ignited his bass amplifier
To protest Fred Durst and Limp Bizkit winning Best Rock Video over them
fact: Frustrated that Limp Bizkit took home the moonman, Commerford scaled the backdrop truss during Limp Bizkit's speech, refusing to come down until security removed him, resulting in a night in jail.

q: Which rock superstar was bitten by a bat, swallowed live goldfish, and once reportedly bit the head off a live dove during an executive board meeting at CBS Records in London?
fact: To make a memorable impression on record executives in 1981, Sharon Osbourne planned for Ozzy to release two white doves into the air; instead, an intoxicated Ozzy bit one dove's head off and spat it onto the table.

q: In 1974, John Lennon was forcibly ejected from The Troubadour nightclub in West Hollywood alongside singer Harry Nilsson after Lennon did what?
options: Threw a martini into Jerry Lee Lewis's piano
Stripped to his socks and challenged the bartender to a boxing match
Affixed an unused Kotex sanitary napkin to his forehead and heckled the Smothers Brothers
Smashed the venue's plate-glass front window with a beer bottle
fact: During his infamous 18-month "Lost Weekend" in Los Angeles, Lennon put a sanitary pad on his head, asked a waitress if she knew who he was, and loudly disrupted Tommy and Dick Smothers' comedy set.

q: In 2011, which famous actor woke up in the middle of the night at his Orange County home to find a naked man standing by his bed wearing only his leather jacket and eating a bag of Fritos?
fact: Nicolas Cage recounted that he woke up in his Newport Beach house at 2:00 AM to see an intruder standing in his bedroom wearing Cage's leather jacket and munching on corn chips; Cage calmly talked him out of the house until police arrived.

q: Why did Keith Moon once dress as Adolf Hitler and hire a German shepherd to march around London's Jewish neighborhood of Golders Green?
options: He was filming a scene for Monty Python
He lost a high-stakes poker bet to Oliver Reed
He had an abrasive, anarchic sense of humor and did it entirely as a bizarre shock prank
He was protesting British censorship laws
fact: Keith Moon loved shocking the public with tasteless costumes; he once rented a full Nazi officer uniform and open-top Mercedes to drive through Jewish neighborhoods in London, nearly sparking a riot.

q: Which legendary actor was so notoriously combative on the set of "Alien 3" that director David Fincher was forced to paint a green tennis ball on a stand for Sigourney Weaver to act against instead?
fact: While Charles Dance was notoriously candid about his frustrations with studio interference, Fincher frequently had to use physical markers like painted tennis balls for creature sightlines because the practical alien rigs were constantly malfunctioning.

q: In 1993, while filming "Groundhog Day" in Woodstock, Illinois, Bill Murray was bitten twice by the groundhog playing Punxsutawney Phil. What did doctors have to administer?
fact: The temperamental groundhog (named Scooter) disliked Murray intensely and bit him deeply on the hand twice during shooting, requiring Murray to undergo precautionary rabies shots.

q: In 2005, Prince surprised the comedy troupe of "Chappelle's Show" by using which image as the official single cover artwork for his song "Breakfast Can Wait"?
options: An unreleased photo from his 1984 Purple Rain tour
A Polaroid taken inside a Minneapolis diner
A cartoon drawing by Matt Groening
Dave Chappelle dressed as Prince serving pancakes
fact: Prince famously loved Dave Chappelle's legendary sketch depicting him playing basketball and serving pancakes; years later, Prince made Chappelle's pancake-holding portrait the official cover of his 2013 single.

q: In 2015, which country's Deputy Prime Minister threatened to have Johnny Depp's Yorkshire terriers, Pistol and Boo, euthanized after they were illegally flown in on a private jet?
fact: Australian Agriculture Minister Barnaby Joyce gave Depp and Amber Heard a 50-hour ultimatum to remove their dogs from Australia or face their destruction due to strict national biosecurity laws.

q: What bizarre culinary obsession did Alfred Hitchcock have when hosting formal dinner parties at his Bel-Air mansion?
options: He forced all guests to eat using only surgical scalpels
He served courses entirely in reverse, starting with coffee and ending with cold oysters
He placed fake rubber flies into the bottom of every soup bowl
He insisted that every course, including the meat and soup, be dyed bright blue
fact: Hitchcock was known for macabre practical jokes, notably hosting a famous dinner where all food—including steaks, potatoes, sauces, and dessert—was dyed blue with food coloring to disturb guests.

q: Which rock band was banned for life from "Saturday Night Live" in 1986 after their lead singer smashed the stage camera and began violently trashing the studio set?
fact: The Replacements showed up thoroughly intoxicated, traded clothes between songs, shouted profanities on live television, and trashed backstage dressing rooms, earning a lifetime ban from Lorne Michaels.

q: In 1998, which movie star punched a paparazzo who tried to photograph him having dinner with Leonardo DiCaprio and then claimed to police that his hand had "merely made contact with a fly"?
fact: Sean Penn's notorious temper with paparazzi led to multiple violent confrontations throughout the 1980s and 1990s, including arrests and jail time for assaulting photographers.

q: What unusual pet did Salvador Dalí bring along on his visit to the St. Regis hotel in New York, which he tied to his desk in the hotel suite?
fact: Dalí traveled extensively with his beloved pet ocelot, Babou, taking him into restaurants and hotels across New York and Paris on a jewel-encrusted collar and leash.

q: During a heated argument on the set of the 1999 movie "Any Given Sunday", director Oliver Stone had to break up an actual fistfight between Jamie Foxx and which co-star?
fact: The intense rivalry between Foxx's and LL Cool J's characters spilled over into real life; during a scrimmage scene, LL Cool J hit Foxx for real, leading Foxx to punch back before Miami police were called.

q: Which celebrated writer lived with more than 50 polydactyl (six-toed) cats at his estate in Key West, Florida, whose descendants still roam the grounds today?
fact: Hemingway was gifted a six-toed white kitten named Snow White by a sea captain; today, dozens of direct polydactyl descendants live protected at the Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum.

q: In 1974, David Bowie reportedly survived for months on an extreme diet consisting entirely of which three items?
options: Celery stalks, black coffee, and vodka
Red peppers, raw milk, and cocaine
Canned sardines, black tea, and amphetamines
fact: Bowie later confessed that during the recording of "Station to Station" in Los Angeles, his daily intake was reduced almost exclusively to red peppers, full-fat milk, and heavy amounts of cocaine.

q: In 1984, which hard rock frontman accidentally caught his own hair on fire while filming a lavish MTV music video featuring indoor pyrotechnics?
fact: While filming a Pepsi commercial at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles in January 1984, pyrotechnics detonated early, igniting Michael Jackson's hair and causing severe second- and third-degree scalp burns.

q: Which classic film director owned a fully functional miniature live-steam locomotive in his backyard that was large enough for adults to ride on?
fact: Walt Disney built the Carolwood Pacific Railroad, a 1:8 scale rideable live-steam railroad that looped 2,615 feet around his Holmby Hills estate, inspiring the creation of the Disneyland Railroad.

q: In 2004, which eccentric actor purchased an authentic, complete medieval knight's suit of armor and a two-headed snake for his private residence?
fact: Cage's famous spending sprees included a $276,000 two-headed snake named Harvey, shrunken pygmy heads, a 9-foot burial pyramid in New Orleans, and ancient armor.

q: Why did country music outlaw Waylon Jennings walk out of the historic 1985 "We Are the World" recording session at A&M Studios?
options: He refused to share a microphone with Bob Dylan
He got into a fistfight with Cyndi Lauper
He was angry that Michael Jackson was wearing sunglasses indoors
He refused to sing lines translated into Swahili
fact: When Stevie Wonder suggested including lines in Swahili to connect with famine relief, Jennings famously declared, "No good old boy sings in Swahili," packed his guitar, and walked out.

q: What did actor Gary Busey do during a live television red-carpet interview at the 2008 Academy Awards that completely stunned Ryan Seacrest and Laura Linney?
options: He crashed the interview uninvited, hugged Linney from behind, and kissed her neck
He shoved Seacrest to the floor and grabbed the microphone
He took out a raw potato from his tuxedo and took a bite
He barked like a dog for three straight minutes into the lens
fact: Busey interrupted Seacrest mid-interview, wrapped his arms around a visibly stunned Linney, and proceeded to kiss her neck on live television before wandering off.

q: Which comedy icon made a guest appearance on "Late Night with David Letterman" in 1982 wearing a neck brace and proceeded to slap guest host Andy Kaufman off his chair?
fact: Professional wrestler Jerry Lawler appeared alongside Kaufman following their Memphis wrestling feud; Lawler slapped Kaufman off his chair, sparking a curse-laden live TV tirade.

q: In 1969, John Lennon and Yoko Ono protested the Vietnam War by remaining in bed for two weeks in presidential suites in which two cities?
options: London and New York during the notorious incident
fact: The couple staged their famous "Bed-Ins for Peace" at the Hilton Hotel in Amsterdam and the Queen Elizabeth Hotel in Montreal, where they also recorded "Give Peace a Chance".

q: In 1997, which professional boxer infamously bit off a chunk of his opponent's ear during a world championship rematch in Las Vegas?
fact: During round three of their rematch at the MGM Grand, Tyson bit off a one-inch piece of Evander Holyfield's right ear cartilage, resulting in a disqualification and revoked boxing license.

q: What did surrealist painter Salvador Dalí do when invited to deliver a lecture at the London International Surrealist Exhibition in 1936?
options: He spoke while floating in a glass tank filled with red dye
He rode onto the podium on a live white horse
He delivered the speech inside a deep-sea diving suit and nearly suffocated
He gave the entire lecture in sign language despite not knowing sign language
fact: Dalí wanted to demonstrate that he was "plunging deep into the human subconscious," but the airtight diving helmet bolted shut, and he began suffocating until friends pried it open with a billiard cue.

q: Which famous comedian was arrested in Chicago in 1962 for violating obscenity laws after saying the word "schmuck" on stage at the Gate of Horn nightclub?
fact: Bruce faced relentless legal persecution throughout the early 1960s; during his December 1962 arrest in Chicago, police targeted his use of Yiddish profanity and sexual satire.

q: Which movie star broke two ribs while filming the famous tavern fight scene in "The Bourne Supremacy" because he refused to use a stunt double?
fact: Matt Damon performed many of his own intense hand-to-hand fight sequences under the choreography of Jeff Imada, suffering multiple bruises, cuts, and cracked ribs during production.

q: What bizarre gift did Angelina Jolie and Billy Bob Thornton notoriously exchange and wear as necklaces around their necks during their marriage in the early 2000s?
options: Silver lockets containing droplets of each other’s blood
Shards of a meteorite they found in Nevada
The wisdom teeth of their childhood pets
Glass vials containing ashes of their wedding vows
fact: The eccentric couple made headlines worldwide by wearing matching vials filled with drops of each other's blood on silver chains around their necks.

q: In 1978, which member of The Rolling Stones was arrested by the Royal Canadian Mounted Police after being caught with an ounce of heroin in his Toronto hotel suite?
fact: Richards faced life imprisonment under Canadian narcotics laws; his sentence was reduced to playing two benefit concerts for the Canadian National Institute for the Blind.

q: Which actor was arrested in 1993 outside the Viper Room in West Hollywood after getting into a brawl with a photographer who tried to capture River Phoenix’s final moments?
fact: Flea, who had been performing on stage with Phoenix that night, accompanied Phoenix in the ambulance and clashed with paparazzi gathering outside the venue.

q: In 1987, which actor accidentally killed two women in an automobile collision while vacationing in Northern Ireland?
fact: Broderick was driving a rented BMW on the wrong side of the road in Enniskillen, Northern Ireland, when he collided head-on with a vehicle carrying Anna Gallagher and Margaret Doherty, both of whom died.

q: What unusual animal did Michael Jackson purchase from a Texas research facility in the mid-1980s that accompanied him on his "Bad" world tour?
fact: Jackson acquired Bubbles in 1985; the chimpanzee lived at Neverland Valley Ranch, slept in a crib in Jackson's bedroom, and traveled with him to Japan during the 1987 Bad tour.

q: In 1980, which rock frontwoman was arrested for throwing a bottle of Dom Pérignon through the plate-glass window of a hotel lobby in Frankfurt?
fact: Slick's alcohol-fueled outbursts with Jefferson Starship were legendary; during a disastrous 1978 German tour, she repeatedly mocked crowds with Nazi references and destroyed hotel furnishings.

q: Which Golden Age actress was so obsessed with cleanliness that she reportedly cleaned every surface of hotel rooms with rubbing alcohol and made guests take off their shoes outside her dressing room?
fact: Crawford suffered from severe germaphobia and obsessive-compulsive traits, scrubbing bathroom tiles herself with bleach and covering all furniture in plastic wrap.

q: Which rock musician once hired a crane to drop an old grand piano out of a helicopter into a gravel quarry just to record the acoustic reverberation of the crash?
fact: Frank Zappa was famous for avant-garde acoustic experiments and musique concrète, capturing ambient explosions, smashing instruments, and recording mechanical cacophony for sound textures.

q: What did actor Joaquin Phoenix do during his bizarre February 2009 appearance on "Late Show with David Letterman"?
options: He laid down across the guest chairs and pretended to sleep
He challenged Paul Shaffer to an arm-wrestling contest
He announced his retirement from acting to become a hip-hop artist and gave monosyllabic answers behind dark sunglasses
He refused to speak and communicated solely through handwritten cards
fact: Phoenix stayed completely in-character for his mockumentary "I'm Still Here", sporting an unkempt beard, mumbling incoherently, and sticking his chewing gum under Letterman's desk.

q: Which celebrated actor once challenged a real bear to a wrestling match inside a circular pit at a German carnival while studying at the Bristol Old Vic?
fact: The booming British actor Brian Blessed, known for larger-than-life physical feats, wrestled a declawed brown bear at a Bavarian festival in his youth and emerged victorious.

q: In 1965, which singer-songwriter was struck by lightning while on a golf course in North Carolina and walked away with minor burns?
fact: Golf champion Lee Trevino survived a direct lightning strike at the 1975 Western Open at Butler National Golf Club, suffering spine injuries that required corrective surgery.

q: Which musician was once rescued from drowning in the Mississippi River after attempting to swim across it in full clothing while intoxicated?
fact: Tragically, singer-songwriter Jeff Buckley drowned in May 1997 after wading into the Wolf River harbor, an offshoot of the Mississippi River, while singing Led Zeppelin's "Whole Lotta Love" with his boots on.

q: What did legendary rock guitarist Jimi Hendrix do to his Fender Stratocaster at the climax of his performance at the 1967 Monterey Pop Festival?
options: Smashed it into the bass drum and tossed it into the Pacific Ocean
Cut all the strings with wire cutters using his teeth
Doused it in lighter fluid, set it on fire, and smashed it against the stage
Threw it like a javelin through the stage backdrop
fact: To outdo The Who's instrument-destroying finale earlier that day, Hendrix knelt over his guitar, squirted lighter fluid on it, struck a match, and theatrically sacrificed it to the flames.

q: In 1983, which actor broke his leg while jumping out of an attic window to escape an angry husband who arrived home unexpectedly?
fact: Beatty’s legendary romantic escapades occasionally had dangerous exits; over the decades, several close calls involving jealous partners and balconies became staples of Hollywood lore.

q: What eccentric request did actor Peter Sellers make regarding the color purple on all film sets he worked on?
options: He demanded that all his costumes contain at least one shade of purple
He had an intense phobia of the color purple and green, refusing to step onto any set containing them
He insisted his dressing room walls be painted deep royal purple
He required all crew members to wear purple wristbands
fact: Sellers had deep occult superstitions and a profound phobia of the colors purple and green, believing they brought misfortune and death; he refused to act in scenes where purple clothing appeared.

q: In 1995, which heavy metal vocalist was rushed to the hospital after biting into a raw sheep heart thrown on stage during a performance in Mexico City?
fact: Danzig frequently incorporated gory stage aesthetics; during an unruly show in South America, an audience member threw an animal heart which he bit, leading to an emergency hospital visit for bacterial infection.

q: Which famous musician legally changed his name to an unpronounceable "Love Symbol" in 1993 to rebel against Warner Bros. Records?
fact: Frustrated by contractual disputes over the ownership of his master recordings, Prince adopted the unpronounceable glyph, leading journalists to call him "The Artist Formerly Known as Prince".

q: In 1975, which movie star walked onto the set of "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" having had an actual electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) session to prepare for his role?
fact: Nicholson underwent a mock ECT procedure with medical supervision to accurately replicate the muscular spasms and disorientation experienced by McMurphy in the film.

q: Which legendary comedian famously carried around a fake severed thumb in his pocket to drop into strangers' drinks at cocktail parties?
fact: Dangerfield loved corny practical jokes, frequently dropping a rubber thumb into drinks or slipping trick novelties into dinner guests' pockets to break the tension.

q: In 1992, which pop star caused international outrage by tearing up a photograph of Pope John Paul II on live television during a performance on "Saturday Night Live"?
fact: At the end of an a cappella performance of Bob Marley's "War", O'Connor tore up a photo of the Pope and told viewers to "fight the real enemy" to protest child sexual abuse within the Catholic Church.

q: Which Hollywood actor bought a 19th-century church in England, had it dismantled stone by stone, and had it shipped to his estate in Malibu to use as a guest house?
fact: Mel Gibson, an adherent of traditionalist Catholicism, purchased historical European stonework and historic chapel pieces to build his own private parish, Holy Family Church, in the hills of Agoura Hills near Malibu.

q: In 1994, which actor trashed a $1,200-a-night presidential suite at New York's Mark Hotel, blaming the damage on a mythical rogue armadillo?
fact: Depp was arrested for criminal mischief after security found shattered glass and wrecked furniture; he claimed a rogue armadillo had popped out of the closet and went on a rampage.

q: In 1972, which legendary singer was arrested in Houston, Texas, after police found him walking down a street with a loaded pistol and a paper sack containing $30,000 in cash?
fact: Sly Stone's eccentric, drug-fueled behavior reached extreme heights in the early 1970s, frequently carrying firearms, stacks of cash, and pet pit bulls everywhere he went.

q: Why did actor Daniel Day-Lewis refuse to leave his wheelchair and demand that crew members feed him with a spoon during production of "My Left Foot" (1989)?
options: He broke his hip on the first day of shooting
He suffered a severe case of psychosomatic paralysis
The director bet him $10,000 he couldn't do it for two months during the notorious incident
To remain immersed in the physical limitations of Christy Brown
fact: Day-Lewis stayed strictly in character around the clock, forcing annoyed crew members to lift him over camera cables, carry him up stairs, and spoon-feed him meals.

q: In 1988, which legendary funk and soul superstar led police on a two-state interstate car chase that ended after officers shot out his truck's tires?
fact: James Brown barged into an insurance office with a shotgun complaining about bathroom use, then led Georgia and South Carolina police on a high-speed chase, resulting in a six-year prison sentence.

q: During the filming of "The Shining", which actress was pushed to such psychological and physical exhaustion by director Stanley Kubrick that her hair began falling out in clumps?
fact: Kubrick forced Duvall to perform the baseball bat staircase scene an astonishing 127 times, keeping her under continuous manufactured distress for over a year.

q: In 1964, which classic Hollywood hardman was arrested after shooting a hole through the floor of his private chartered airplane because the pilot refused to turn up the cabin heat?
fact: World War II veteran Lee Marvin was notorious for heavy-drinking escapades; during one turbulent flight, he shot through the floorboards to get the cockpit crew's immediate attention.

q: Which rock star reportedly spent thousands of dollars to fly his favorite hat first-class from London to Rome when he realized he forgot it?
fact: In 2003, Bono realized he had left his favorite black trilby hat in London before an Italian benefit concert with Pavarotti, paying roughly £1,000 to fly the hat in its own first-class seat on British Airways.

q: In 1999, which British pop star was rescued by local villagers after his yacht caught fire and sank off the coast of Saint-Tropez?
fact: Rod Stewart and his family had to scramble into emergency lifeboats when their luxury chartered cruiser caught fire in the Mediterranean, being rescued by nearby French fishing boats.

q: What eccentric thing did screen icon Cary Grant legally experiment with over 100 times in the late 1950s under psychiatric supervision in California?
fact: Grant underwent more than 60 supervised sessions of clinical LSD therapy in Beverly Hills, crediting the hallucinogen with helping him overcome childhood trauma and find inner peace.

q: Which actor stayed in a remote Canadian wilderness cabin for weeks eating raw bison liver and sleeping inside an animal carcass to prepare for his Oscar-winning role?
fact: While filming "The Revenant", DiCaprio—a strict vegetarian—chose to eat real raw bison liver on camera and endured freezing temperatures inside animal pelts.

q: In 1985, which pop icon rode a mechanical bull into a private VIP birthday party thrown at Studio 54?
fact: Grace Jones was famous for dramatic and hyper-physical nightclub entries, frequently roaring into venues astride bulls, motorcycles, or atop muscular bodybuilders.

q: Why did author Roald Dahl have all the teeth removed from his mouth at age 21?
options: Severe battlefield scurvy in North Africa
A bet with fellow author Ian Fleming
A horrific plane crash shattered his entire jaw
He believed artificial dentures were far more efficient and never required brushing
fact: Dahl had all his natural teeth pulled in his early twenties simply because he considered human teeth an unnecessary maintenance nuisance, proudly wearing false dentures thereafter.

q: Which eccentric actor bought a historic 18th-century English castle, along with an allegedly haunted Bavarian castle (Schloss Neustein), contributing to his famous financial collapse?
fact: Cage bought Midford Castle in Somerset, England, and Schloss Neidstein in Germany in the mid-2000s as part of an extravagant international real estate buying spree.

q: In 1977, which member of Pink Floyd spat directly into the face of an unruly fan leaning over the front barrier during a stadium show in Montreal?
fact: Waters grew so disgusted by the alienation and rowdiness of stadium rock crowds that he spat on a shouting fan in Montreal; the guilt and isolation from that moment directly inspired the album "The Wall".

q: What bizarre prop did Peter O'Toole and Omar Sharif notoriously take with them to the casino while shooting "Lawrence of Arabia" in the Jordanian desert?
options: A live golden eagle on a leather gauntlet
Two burlap sacks containing millions of French francs
A bucket of dry martini mixers
fact: Bored during production breaks in Beirut, O'Toole and Sharif famously visited casinos with bags of cash, with Sharif once losing his entire salary for the movie in a single night of roulette.

q: In 1996, which eccentric rock star walked off stage at the Reading Festival after the audience pelted the band with plastic bottles, mud, and raw meat?
fact: Meat Loaf and his band were bombarded with bottles and debris by a hostile alternative-rock crowd; after getting struck by a full two-liter cider bottle, he stormed off the stage.

q: What unusual pet did Audrey Hepburn have that used to follow her through Beverly Hills grocery stores and accompanied her to film studios?

q: Which Oscar-winning actor spent six months living on the streets of London in ragged clothes to research his role as a homeless pianist?
fact: Brody gave up his car, his New York apartment, his cell phone, and starved himself down to 130 pounds to connect with the desolate isolation of Władysław Szpilman in "The Pianist".

q: In 1973, which rock icon was arrested in a Memphis hotel room after shooting his own manager's watch off his wrist with a target pistol?
fact: "The Killer" Jerry Lee Lewis was notorious for handling loaded firearms while heavily intoxicated; on another occasion, he accidentally shot his bass player Norman Owens in the chest.

q: Which famous British author wrote almost all of his best-selling novels while lying flat on his back in bed with a wooden board across his lap?
fact: Proust lived as a reclusive asthmatic invalid in a cork-lined bedroom in Paris, drafting his monumental multi-volume masterpiece "In Search of Lost Time" almost entirely while propped up in bed.

q: In 2002, which pop superstar held his nine-month-old son Prince Michael II (Blanket) over a fourth-floor hotel balcony railing in Berlin to show him to fans?
fact: Standing on the balcony of the Hotel Adlon in Berlin, Jackson dangled his infant son over the railing with one arm, causing worldwide panic and intense media criticism.

q: Which Hollywood star was blacklisted from renting cars across California after he repeatedly drove rental sports cars into swimming pools at Palm Springs motels in the 1960s?
fact: Keith Moon's legendary habit of sinking vehicles into motel pools—including a Lincoln Continental and several Lincolns/Cadillacs—cost The Who hundreds of thousands of dollars in property damage.

q: What did actor Christopher Walken insist on doing to the script pages of every screenplay he was ever given before agreeing to film a scene?
options: Re-typing them on a vintage manual typewriter
Burning the corners with a cigarette lighter
Translating them into German and back into English
Crossing out all punctuation marks so he could invent his own speech cadence
fact: Walken famously eliminated all periods, commas, and question marks from his scripts, allowing him to create his trademark erratic, unpredictable vocal rhythm and pauses.

q: In 1969, why was actress Jane Fonda arrested at Cleveland Hopkins International Airport on suspicion of drug trafficking?
options: She had prescription tranquilizers in unmarked pill bottles
She hid marijuana brownies inside film canisters
She carried vials of experimental vitamins labeled with B, C, and D
She was framed by undercover FBI agents
fact: Fonda was detained by customs when officers found bottles of dietary vitamin pills; mugshots of her raising a defiant clenched fist became an enduring cultural image of 1970s activism.

q: Which celebrated actor reportedly challenged British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher to an arm-wrestling match at a Downing Street reception?
fact: The famously bellicose Oliver Reed regularly challenged politicians, journalists, and fellow actors to arm-wrestle, famously propositioning the Iron Lady herself during a state reception.

q: In 1982, which country legend was arrested after landing an airplane on a public highway near Nashville because he had run out of fuel?
fact: George Jones' battles with alcohol were notorious; when his wife hid his car keys, he famously drove his John Deere riding lawnmower eight miles into town to buy liquor.

q: Which rock star had his portrait painted in his own blood by artist Pete Doherty while staying in a London rehabilitation clinic?
fact: Doherty created a miniature self-portrait alongside Amy Winehouse titled "Ladylike", painted using droplets of their own blood smeared with hypodermic syringes.

q: What unusual item did actor Marlon Brando keep in a display cabinet in his living room, claiming it was his most prized possession?
options: Al Pacino’s real high school diploma
An uncashed $10,000 check signed by Charlie Chaplin
A jar containing kidney stones passed by Jack Nicholson
fact: Chaplin directed Brando in "A Countess from Hong Kong" (1967); despite their mutual hatred on set, Brando framed Chaplin's uncashed personal check as a tribute to Chaplin's comic genius.

q: In 1991, which Guns N' Roses member sparked a massive riot at the Riverport Amphitheatre near St. Louis after diving into the crowd to confiscate a fan's camera?
fact: Axl slammed his microphone down, shouted "Thanks to the lame-ass security, I'm going home!", and walked off; the resulting riot caused over $200,000 in venue damage and left dozens injured.

q: What did eccentric director Werner Herzog do when film student Errol Morris successfully completed and premiered his documentary "Gates of Heaven"?

Boiled and ate his own leather shoe on camera
Shaved his head completely bald in front of the audience

q: In 1980, which comedian faked his own arrest by hiring two actors dressed as policemen to drag him out of a live taping of "The Merv Griffin Show"?
fact: Kaufman loved breaking the fourth wall; he frequently orchestrated fake physical brawls, nervous breakdowns, and scripted police raids during talk show appearances.

q: Which actress famously broke two toes during the filming of "The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers" after angrily kicking an iron orc helmet?

q: Which movie superstar bought a real Russian MiG-29 fighter jet and flew it across European airspace for personal recreation?

q: In 1995, which Oasis frontman showed up at an awards ceremony wearing a football jersey and proceeded to flick beer bottle caps at Blur singer Damon Albarn?
fact: At the height of the "Battle of Britpop", Liam Gallagher constantly provoked Damon Albarn and Graham Coxon at industry events, taunting them with vulgar chants and flying beer caps.

q: What did surrealist master Salvador Dalí send as an official wedding gift to pop icon Cher and her husband Gregg Allman in 1975?
options: A customized diamond-studded replica human skull
An antique silver spoon bent in half
A plaster mold of his own mustache
A gilded birdcage filled with dead beetles
fact: Dalí was notorious for sending disturbing or macabre gifts to high-profile friends, once gifting Cher a display case filled with mounted exotic dead insects.

q: In 1971, which iconic country star was trapped inside an airplane bathroom for three hours because the door lock jammed during a flight to Las Vegas?
fact: Parton was trapped in the tiny lavatory; the flight crew had to dismantle the door hinges with butter knives and screwdrivers while she sang gospel songs from inside to keep calm.

q: Which famous comedian got into an armed standoff with federal marshals inside a Beverly Hills bank vault in 1977 after refusing to hand over cash to his ex-wife?
fact: "Sanford and Son" star Redd Foxx fought brutal, public tax and divorce battles; during one IRS raid, he barricaded himself in a safe-deposit vault to keep his jewelry.

q: In 1968, which Beatles member temporarily quit the band during the "White Album" sessions and flew to Sardinia on actor Peter Sellers' yacht?
fact: Feeling unappreciated and alienated by the tense studio fighting, Ringo announced he was leaving the Beatles; while vacationing in Sardinia, he wrote "Octopus's Garden" before returning.

q: What bizarre medical souvenir did actress Angelina Jolie give to her brother James Haven as a token of sibling affection?
options: Her childhood baby teeth inside an antique silver locket
A glass vial filled with her own appendectomy fluids
A framed copy of her brain MRI
Her extracted wisdom teeth set in gold rings

q: In 1993, which action superstar accidentally shot through the roof of a limousine in Beverly Hills while demonstrating a handgun to film executives?
fact: Seagal frequently carried concealed handguns on film sets and business meetings; multiple stunt performers and executives have documented accidental discharges and near-misses during his demonstrations.

q: Which legendary actress was once detained by customs at Rome Airport for attempting to board a flight with a cheetah cub tucked under her fur coat?
fact: Passionate animal activist Brigitte Bardot frequently rescued exotic wildlife in the 1960s and 1970s, causing multiple international airport scandals by carrying undocumented animals onto planes.

q: Which classic rock singer once had an entire hotel swimming pool drained because he dropped a diamond-encrusted Rolex into the deep end and refused to dive for it?
fact: Elton John’s lavish lifestyle in the 1970s included paying luxury resorts exorbitant fees to drain entire Olympic-sized pools so bellhops could retrieve his dropped jewelry.

q: In 1981, which movie star punched director Sydney Pollack in the face during a heated argument over the final cut of the comedy "Tootsie"?
fact: Hoffman and Pollack fought constantly over tone and character realism throughout the shoot; Hoffman frequently stormed out and shoved Pollack during shouting matches on set.

q: What did actor Sean Penn do to an intrusive paparazzi helicopter hovering over his outdoor Malibu wedding to Madonna in 1985?

Fired a flare gun toward the aircraft
Threw rocks at the helicopter skids
Carved giant expletives into the sand on the beach below

q: In 1998, which legendary musician was kicked off an airplane in Melbourne, Australia, after lighting a cigarette and blowing smoke directly into a flight attendant's face?
fact: Liam Gallagher’s drunken air rage was notorious; Cathay Pacific banned him for life after he threw scones, shouted obscenities, and smoked on a flight to Australia.

q: Which famous writer challenged boxing champion Jack Johnson to a sparring match in Paris in 1913 and had several front teeth knocked out in round one?
fact: Cravan, the Dadaist poet, amateur boxer, and nephew of Oscar Wilde, staged a legendary 1916 exhibition bout in Barcelona against heavyweight champion Jack Johnson, who knocked him out cold in the sixth round.

q: What did British eccentric Keith Moon do when a police officer pulled him over for speeding in his Rolls-Royce?

Stripped naked and locked himself inside the trunk
Handed the officer a £100 note and sped away without saying a word
Replaced the steering wheel with a large sausage

q: In 1999, which superstar singer survived an emergency landing when his private plane overshot the runway in Jamaica and plunged into a swamp?

q: Which movie star notoriously paid $276,000 at a Beverly Hills auction for a rare 19th-century murder weapon: the walking stick of Jack the Ripper?
fact: Nicolas Cage's legendary appetite for macabre historical artifacts led him to purchase authentic Victorian crime memorabilia, rare oddities, and historical murder relics.

q: In 1994, which actor attacked a car windshield with a golf club in a fit of road rage at an intersection in North Hollywood?
fact: Nicholson grabbed a two-iron from his trunk and smashed the windshield and roof of a Mercedes whose driver had reportedly cut him off in traffic; the civil suit was settled out of court.

q: Which legendary actress was famously pulled over for slapping Beverly Hills police officer Paul Ellis during a routine traffic stop in 1989?
fact: Gabor was stopped for driving an unregistered Rolls-Royce with an open container of alcohol; when confronted, she slapped the officer, leading to a high-profile trial and a 3-day jail term.

q: What did actor Steve Buscemi famously do in the days immediately following the September 11 terrorist attacks in New York City?

Flew private supply helicopters into lower Manhattan
Organized an impromptu benefit concert in Central Park
Staged a 48-hour live radio marathon to raise funds
fact: Buscemi, who worked as an FDNY firefighter in the 1980s, returned to his old firehouse in Little Italy, working 12-hour shifts alongside former colleagues at Ground Zero without seeking media attention.

q: In 1982, why did Ozzy Osbourne get arrested in San Antonio, Texas, resulting in a decade-long ban from performing in the city?
options: For throwing fireworks from his tour bus into city hall
For urinating on the Alamo cenotaph while wearing one of Sharon's dresses
For biting the head off a toy bat during a live radio broadcast
For attempting to climb the walls of the Alamo fort

q: Which Hollywood superstar was famously an elite competitive diver on the British National Diving Squad, placing 12th at the 1992 World Championships?
fact: Before launching his acting career with "Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels", Statham spent 12 years on the British National Diving Squad and competed in the 1990 Commonwealth Games.

q: In 1969, which actress and sex symbol reportedly demanded that 100 gallons of whole cow's milk be heated daily so she could take skin-rejuvenating baths in hotel tubs?
fact: Mansfield was famous for outlandish promotional antics and luxury indulgences, regularly claiming to take warm milk baths and living in the iconic, all-pink "Pink Palace" on Sunset Boulevard.

q: Which Grammy-winning artist was shot nine times at point-blank range outside his grandmother’s house in Queens in May 2000 and miraculously survived?
fact: Jackson survived shots to his hand, arm, hip, both legs, chest, and face, with a bullet fragment lodging permanently in his tongue, altering his distinct vocal cadence.

q: What bizarre medical request did Keith Richards make regarding his skull after falling out of a palm tree in Fiji in 2006?
options: He asked the surgeon to preserve the bone shavings as guitar picks
He asked the doctor if he could keep the drill bit used to relieve his hematoma
He refused general anesthesia unless his personal stash was administered
He demanded to be conscious during brain surgery so he could supervise

q: In 1984, which famous musician brought a live llama into a recording studio, prompting Freddie Mercury to cancel their planned duet sessions?
fact: Mercury was recording duets with Michael Jackson at Jackson's home studio in Encino; Mercury called his manager pleading to leave because Jackson insisted on keeping his pet llama, Louie, in the studio.

q: Which British actor served as an uncredited secret intelligence and reconnaissance officer during World War II, tracking Nazi war criminals across post-war Europe?
fact: Lee was attached to the SAS, RAF intelligence, and the Central Registry of War Criminals and Security Suspects, personally interviewing captured Nazi commanders and helping apprehend war criminals.

q: In 1997, which movie star bought a $200,000 vintage Russian tank and legally drove it through the streets of his Wiltshire estate to blow off steam?
fact: Schwarzenegger bought the exact Austrian army tank (an M47 Patton) that he drove during his compulsory military service in 1965, shipping it to California to crush junked cars for charity events.

q: Why was silent film star Buster Keaton known as "The Great Stone Face"?
options: He had permanent facial nerve paralysis from a stunt accident
He wore heavy porcelain face powder during all public appearances
He made a conscious comedic choice to maintain an absolute deadpan expression, never smiling on camera
He sustained a broken jaw during childhood circus acrobatics
fact: Keaton noticed during his vaudeville years with his parents that the audience laughed harder when he showed zero emotion while enduring slapstick abuse, creating his trademark deadpan persona.

q: In 1971, which iconic soul singer flew to Gary, Indiana, and bought a home for his mother, but had to flee after gunfire erupted outside a local venue?
fact: Gaye's career and personal life were marked by intense family and criminal tensions; his chaotic regional tours in the early 1970s frequently encountered armed clashes and threats from promoters.

q: In 1986, which actor took a real live goat as his date to a premiere afterparty in Hollywood, claiming it was his "life advisor"?
fact: Glover's legendary off-screen eccentricities included eccentric farm animal appearances and strange public performance art throughout the mid-1980s.

q: Which rock icon fell off a stage in London in 1971 after a fan rushed him, breaking his leg, fracturing his skull, and causing a permanent drop in his vocal pitch?
fact: A jealous boyfriend pushed Zappa off the Rainbow Theatre stage into a 15-foot concrete orchestra pit; Zappa spent months in a wheelchair, had one leg heal shorter than the other, and dropped a third in vocal range.

q: In 1993, which actor broke a paparazzo's camera with a baseball bat outside a Manhattan gym, resulting in probation and mandatory anger management?
fact: Baldwin confronted a photographer who was videotaping his wife Kim Basinger and their newborn daughter, leading to a physical tussle that broke the camera lens.

q: Which famous musician had their high school senior yearbook signed by classmate and future president Bill Clinton with the note "To the best sax man in Arkansas"?
fact: Arkansan rockabilly legend Ronnie Hawkins attended high school around the region where young Bill Clinton was an aspiring saxophone player, crossing paths in local music circles.

q: Which screen siren reportedly had her ribs surgically removed in the 1930s to give her the world’s most exaggerated hourglass waistline?
fact: Hollywood lore long claimed Dietrich had molars pulled—and allegedly lower ribs removed—to hollow out her cheekbones and accentuate her razor-sharp waistline under studio lighting.

q: In 1985, which legendary actor drove an ambulance in New York City for several nights incognito to prepare for a role as a paramedic?
fact: Cage did ride-alongs with EMS paramedics in New York to prepare for Paul Schrader's "Bringing Out the Dead", spending nights observing real-world trauma and cardiac rescues.

q: Which classic filmmaker was known to test the emotional resilience of young actresses by locking them in dark closets filled with mechanical birds and snakes?
fact: Hitchcock subjected Tippi Hedren to terrifying practical jokes and real live raven attacks on "The Birds", famously having handlers hurl real terrified birds at her for days on end.

q: In 1975, which pop star survived an assassination attempt at his home in Kingston, Jamaica, where gunmen fired into his kitchen two days before a peace concert?
fact: Marley was wounded in the chest and arm when gunmen raided his 56 Hope Road residence; remarkably, he took the stage at the Smile Jamaica concert 48 hours later.

q: Which Hollywood star was once expelled from high school for driving a motorcycle through the school hallways?

q: What did singer-songwriter Tom Waits do to achieve his gravelly, rusted-iron vocal texture in the late 1970s?

Gargled with cheap bourbon mixed with hot lemon juice
Smoked four packs of non-filter Lucky Strikes daily and screamed into pillows
Consumed tablespoons of baking soda before performances
fact: Waits deliberately cultivated his distinctive, worn baritone through relentless smoking, sleep deprivation, alcohol, and aggressive vocal abuse to evoke old-time bluesmen.

q: Which movie star lived in a 1969 Volkswagen bus parked on the beach in Maui while working at Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. before being discovered by a casting agent?
fact: Pratt lived in a van adorned with a Scooby-Doo decal on the beach in Hawaii, smoking weed and waiting tables, until actress Rae Dawn Chong discovered him and cast him in a short horror movie.

q: In 1980, which comedian arrived at an NBC executive's office on roller skates wearing a pink tutu and hand-delivered his own resignation letter?
fact: Kaufman reveled in anti-humor theatrics; he routinely staged bizarre unscripted encounters at television network offices to subvert traditional entertainment hierarchies.

q: Which rock singer famously dislocated his shoulder on stage during a concert in 1989 and demanded that his roadie pop it back into the socket so he could finish the song?
fact: Black Flag frontman Henry Rollins was notorious for extreme stoicism and raw physical endurance, routinely popping dislocated joints back into place on stage while continuing to scream lyrics.
